summary: The shape of a spread rather than its average — latency, jitter, call duration. A mean of 80ms hides whether that is every call at 80 or half at 20 and half at 140.

figma.note: Drawn on the Charts page as `Chart / Distribution`. The touching bins, the single series colour and the marker down the measured axis are there; the binning and the scale are behaviour and are not.

pairs.dont: Report a single average for a latency or jitter figure and move on.
pairs.do: Show the distribution, and mark the percentile the SLA is written against.
pairs.why: An average is one number standing in for a shape, and the shapes that matter most are the ones it flattens. A bimodal spread — most calls fine, a tail that is not — has the same mean as a tight one centred on the same value, and only one of them is an outage.

pairs.dont: Put the bar chart's gap between the bins.
pairs.do: Let them touch; only the plot edges breathe.
pairs.why: A histogram's x axis is continuous and cut into pieces. A gap says there is something between 20–40ms and 40–60ms, and there is not. The gap on a bar chart means the opposite — those categories really are separate things.

pairs.dont: Draw the threshold across the chart, as a count.
pairs.do: Mark it down the measured axis, where the number anyone quotes actually lives.
pairs.why: On a bar chart a threshold is a count — "no more than 20 failures". On a histogram the counts are incidental; the number in the SLA is on the other axis. A horizontal line here marks a bucket height nobody has an opinion about.

pairs.dont: Colour the bins by their value so the chart runs through the series palette.
pairs.why: Position already carries the order and height already carries the count. Spending the identity channel on a third copy of the same information leaves nothing to tell two distributions apart when they are shown side by side.

a11y: The plot is `aria-hidden`; the bucket counts are carried by a visually-hidden table, one row per bucket with its range as the label.
Each bucket carries its own `title` — the range and the count — so a pointer can read one without a crosshair.
An empty bucket keeps its slot and draws nothing, so a gap in the middle of a spread is visible as a gap rather than closing up.
